episode: Heated Tile Floor, East Bench Master Bath
assessment: This is not a reveal episode. It is a process walkthrough of a heated tile floor going into the East Bench phase 3 master bath, and finished footage runs only 8:54 to 9:17, most of it Mike talking to a locked off camera. A straight reveal tour would have nothing to show. It does carry a strong product and process Short: the Schluter heat mat, the wire, the heated zone map, the floor sensor, the continuity test, tile over the top, and the 85 degree payoff. Every beat plays over a state shot. The source is Mike's edited long cut, so its burned in labels, cold open, cost segments and outro graphics are all fenced off.

project_context.summary: Phase 3 of the East Bench house. The master bath gets an electric heated tile floor on a Schluter heat mat. Mike mapped the heated zones for his tile guy, in front of the vanity, the toilet, and where you step out of the tub, and left out the spots nobody stands. Two sensor leads let the programmable thermostat read the floor temperature. The wire gets a continuity test before tile, then tile is set in thinset with a notched trowel and leveled with clips and wedges.
project_context.segment_choice: One Short, a stage by stage process tour from 1:58 to 9:09, opening on the finished bath and ending on the thermostat at 85.
notes: Not a reveal tour, the episode does not have the finished footage for one.
No cost anywhere in the Short. Mike handles cost with his own end slides.

shorts.full_vo: This master bath in the East Bench house got a heated tile floor. Here's how it went in, starting with a Schluter heat mat. The little knobs hold the heating wire, it snaps right in. I drew my tile guy a map of where we wanted heat. In front of the vanity, the toilet, and the tub. Then he ran the wire back and forth through the mat. Two loose wires are a sensor that reads the floor temperature. No heat under the vanity or behind the toilet. Before any tile, you run a continuity test to catch a break. Then the tile goes right on top, set in thinset. Clips and wedges keep every tile flat and level. Now it's set to eighty five, and I can feel it through my feet.
